public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 858

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/858](https://www.erdosproblems.com/858)
- [Er70] Erdős, Paul, _Some extremal problems in combinatorial number theory_. Mathematical Essays
  Dedicated to A. J. Macintyre (1970), 123-133.
- [Al66] Alexander, Ralph, _Density and multiplicative structure of sets of integers_. Acta
  Arith. (1966/67), 321--332.
- [ESS68] Erdős, P. and Sárközi, A. and Szemerédi, E., _On the solvability of certain equations
  in sequences of positive upper logarithmic density_. J. London Math. Soc. (1968), 71--78.
- [Be35] Behrend, F., _On sequences of numbers not divisible by another_. London Math. Soc.
  Journal (1935), 42-45.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos858

/-- `A` has no solution to $at=b$ with $a,b\in A$ and the smallest prime factor of $t$
greater than $a$. -/
def IsAdmissible (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ t : ℕ, a * t = b → t.minFac ≤ a

/-- The maximum of $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$ over all admissible $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$. -/
noncomputable def M (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {m | ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, IsAdmissible A ∧ ∑ n ∈ A, (1 : ℝ) / n = m}

/--
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that there is no solution to $at=b$ with $a,b\in A$ and
the smallest prime factor of $t$ is $>a$. Estimate the maximum of
$$\frac{1}{\log N}\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}.$$

This has been solved by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, who show that for large $N$
$$\max_A \sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=(c+o(1))\log N$$
where the maximum is over all $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with the stated property and
$c\approx 0.618\cdots$ is an explicit constant.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos858.lean#L4771"]
theorem erdos_858 : ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ M N / log N) atTop (nhds c) := by
  sorry

/-- The limit $c\approx 0.618\cdots$ is positive: for any fixed large $N$ the maximum is bounded
away from $0$ (Alexander [Al66], Erdős–Sárközi–Szemerédi [ESS68]). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_858.variants.positive :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ M N / log N) atTop (nhds c) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Alexander [Al66] and Erdős, Sárközi, and Szemerédi [ESS68] proved that if $A$ is an infinite set
with this property then $\sum_{n\in A\cap [1,N]}\frac{1}{n}=o(\log N)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_858.variants.infinite (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (h0 : 0 ∉ A)
    (hadm : ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ t : ℕ, a * t = b → t.minFac ≤ a) :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A), (1 : ℝ) / n) =o[atTop]
      fun N : ℕ ↦ log N := by
  sorry

end Erdos858

findings.description: The theorem asserts only that M(N)/log N converges to some real c. It neither identifies c nor provides an answer slot requesting its value; the positive variant also leaves that value unspecified. This captures a meaningful qualitative part of the solution, but may be insufficient as the main formalization of the source's request to estimate the maximum. Because 'estimate' admits different levels of precision, this is a modelling/coverage concern, not a claim that the theorem is false.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős [Er70], p. 128, asks 'what is the value of' max_A (1/log x) Σ_{a_i<x} 1/a_i (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1970-21.pdf). The exact linked solution identifies a specific limit: its definitions `profile`, `alphaTwo`, and `constant` give an explicit integral formula, and its theorem at line 4771 asserts convergence to that constant, rather than merely existence of a limit (https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos858.lean#L4771).
findings.suggested_fix: Consider defining the explicit constant from the linked solution and stating `Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ M N / log N) atTop (nhds limitConstant)`. Alternatively, pose the requested value using a real-valued `answer(...)` slot as the limit. The present existential convergence theorem can remain as a qualitative variant.

findings.description: The [Be35] bibliography entry gives pages 42–45, but the paper occupies pages 42–44. Its exact title also includes 'one': 'On Sequences of Numbers not Divisible one by another'. No mathematical statement is affected.
findings.source_evidence: Publisher-deposited metadata for DOI 10.1112/jlms/s1-10.37.42 gives the title and pages 42–44 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1112/jlms/s1-10.37.42). The same page range appears in [Er70], reference 3, and [ESS68], reference 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct [Be35] to Behrend, F., 'On sequences of numbers not divisible one by another', J. London Math. Soc. 10 (1935), 42–44.

reformulations.difference: The Lean predicate quantifies over every natural t, without an explicit t > 1 restriction, and expresses the forbidden configuration as an implication with `t.minFac ≤ a`. The linked proof explicitly restricts to t > 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On the positive sets used in the problem, t = 0 cannot satisfy a*t = b, and t = 1 imposes only 1 ≤ a because Nat.minFac 1 = 1. For t > 1, Nat.minFac is the least prime divisor, and `t.minFac ≤ a` is precisely the negation of `a < t.minFac`. Both the explicit-t>1 equivalence and the negated-existence formulation were proved in scratch. The analogous equivalence for the infinite-set predicate was also proved.

reformulations.difference: The source uses a maximum of normalized reciprocal sums, whereas Lean defines a real supremum of unnormalized sums and divides by log N afterwards.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each N the candidate values form a finite nonempty set: there are finitely many subsets of Icc 1 N, and the empty subset supplies value 0. Thus the supremum is an attained maximum, with no default-value issue. For N > 1, log N is positive, so division preserves the maximizing value. Scratch proofs establish both `IsGreatest` for M and `IsGreatest` for M(N)/log N among the normalized candidate sums.

review.notes: All five declarations were checked. Boundary tests proved M(0)=0 and M(1)=1, checked minFac at 0 and 1, and computed equivalent rational maxima through N=13. The infinite-set hypotheses are satisfiable (the primes provide an example), and the little-o conclusion was proved equivalent to vanishing normalized harmonic sums. The exact linked proof and all three non-Mathlib dependencies compiled under Lean 4.33.1; `#print axioms` for its final theorem returned only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The independent problem database also records 858 as solved. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/858 and its forum was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical comparison used the original papers and linked proof; Behrend's PDF was also blocked, but its citation was independently verified. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/proofcheck/. No repository files were modified.
